correctness.rationale: Pinned RESULT.md defines the ordinary Euclidean cubic Steiner polynomial f_h(z)=Ah/3+S_h z+M_h z^2+(4pi/3)z^3 for every fixed full-dimensional planar convex body and arbitrary horizontal apex displacement. Section 1 gives exact volume and lateral-area integral S_h=A+(P/2)h+O(h^-1); section 2 uses the support function max{h_B(u_perp),h u_3} and Cauchy perimeter identity to prove M_h=pi h+pi P/4+O(h^-1) without smoothness hypotheses. Hence f_h/h converges uniformly on compact z to g(z)=pi z^2+Pz/2+A/3, discriminant P^2(1-4Q/3)/4. Continuity of simple roots gives the Q<3/4 vs >3/4 dichotomy. At Q=3/4, z0=-P/(4pi), k(z0)=P^3(3pi-13)/(192pi^2)<0: f_h(z0)<0, neighboring fixed points have positive f_h, forcing two distinct real bounded roots, and rescaling by h^-1/2 yields the precise +/- sqrt(P^3(13-3pi)/(192pi^3 h))+O(h^-1) splitting. Sum of roots gives far root -3h/4+O(1); coefficient positivity makes all real roots negative. Independent SymPy symbolic reduction of critical k and gap matched, and pinned verify.py was inspected for polyhedral face/dihedral sampling. Numeric polygon examples are supplementary; the infinite convex-body statement follows from analytic area/support estimates.
